facts.fact: EcoMatin reports that a ministerial arrete of 27 August 2025 requires Starlink to keep its users' connection logs, IP addresses and traffic data for at least 24 months and to host them locally, on pain of sanctions up to withdrawal of its authorisation.
facts.system: Arrete ministeriel du 27 aout 2025 on Starlink

systems.system: Arrete ministeriel du 27 aout 2025 on Starlink

TCD.note: The arrete only refers to personal data protection provisions in general; no data protection law or its standing is stated.
An October 2024 operator sanction after an internet cut is mentioned without saying the government ordered the cut, and it is outside twelve months.

facts.fact: EcoMatin reports that Starlink services have been authorised in Chad for just two months, and that a ministerial arrete of 27 August 2025 sets conditions on its activity, including identifying customers with the regulator Arcep.
